Function for estimating a Random Effects Poisson-Lindley regression model

Source: R/poisLind.re.R
poisLindRE.Rd

Function for estimating a Random Effects Poisson-Lindley regression model

Usage

poisLind.re(
  formula,
  group_var,
  data,
  method = "NM",
  max.iters = 1000,
  verbose = FALSE,
  stderr = "normal",
  bootstraps = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  keep_data = TRUE,
  print.level = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

an R formula.

group_var

the grouping variable(s) indicating random effects (e.g., individual ID). Required. Several columns are combined into one panel identifier.

data

a dataframe that has all of the variables in the formula.

method

a method to use for optimization in the maximum likelihood estimation. For options, see maxLik. Note that "BHHH" is not available for this function due to the implementation for the random effects.

max.iters

the maximum number of iterations to allow the optimization method to perform.

verbose

logical; if TRUE, print the progress of the optimization.

stderr

the type of standard errors: "normal" (Hessian-based, the default), "robust" (sandwich; clustered by panel because the likelihood has one contribution per panel), or "boot" (bootstrap that resamples whole panels). Giving bootstraps without stderr also requests bootstrapped standard errors.

bootstraps

Optional integer specifying the number of bootstrap samples to be used for estimating standard errors. Whole panels (groups) are resampled, so the standard errors account for the correlation within panels. If not specified, no bootstrapping is performed.

offset

an optional character vector of offset column names (summed when several are given; on the log scale). An offset can instead be given with offset() in formula; use only one of the two.

weights

the name of a column of data, or a numeric vector with one value per row of data, of frequency weights of the panels: a panel with weight w counts as w independent panels in the log-likelihood, the robust covariance, BIC and the bootstrap. Weights must be constant within each panel. Bootstrap standard errors need whole-number weights.

keep_data

logical; if FALSE, the training data are not stored in the fitted object (saving memory). predict() then needs newdata, and fitted()/residuals() are unavailable.

print.level

deprecated; use verbose.

Value

An object of class flexCountReg which is a list with the following components:

  • model: the fitted model object.

  • data: the data frame used to fit the model.

  • call: the matched call.

  • formula: the formula used to fit the model.

Details

poislind_re() is the same function as poisLind.re(), under a name that tools do not mistake for an S3 method.

The function poisLindRE is similar to the poisLind function, but it includes an additional argument group_var that specifies the grouping variable for the random effects. The function estimates a Random Effects Poisson-Lindley regression model using maximum likelihood. It is similar to poisLind, but includes additional terms to account for the random effects.

The Random Effects Poisson-Lindley model is useful for panel data and assumes that the random effects follow a gamma distribution. The PDF is $$ f(y_{it}|\mu_{it},\theta)=\frac{\theta^2}{\theta+1} \prod_{t=1}^{n_i}\frac{\left(\mu_{it}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)} {\theta+2}\right)^{y_{it}}}{y_{it}!} \cdot \frac{ \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{it}\right)! \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\mu_{it}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2} + \theta + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{it} + 1\right) }{ \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\mu_{it}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2} + \theta\right)^{\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{it}+2} } $$

The log-likelihood function is: $$ LL = 2\log(\theta) - \log(\theta+1) + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i} y_{it}\log(\mu_{it}) + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i} y_{it}\log\!\left( \frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2} \right) - \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\log(y_{it}!) + \log\!\left( \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{it}\right)! \right) + \log\!\left( \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\mu_{it}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2} + \theta + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{it} + 1 \right) - \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{it} + 2\right) \log\!\left( \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\mu_{it}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2} + \theta \right) $$

The mean and variance are: $$\mu_{it}=\exp(X_{it} \beta)$$ $$ V(\mu_{it})=\mu_{it}+ \left(1-\frac{2}{(\theta+2)^2}\right)\mu_{it}^2 $$

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
washington_roads$AADTover10k <-
  ifelse(washington_roads$AADT > 10000, 1, 0)

poislind.mod <- poisLind.re(
  Animal ~ lnaadt + lnlength + speed50 +
    ShouldWidth04 + AADTover10k,
  data      = washington_roads,
  group_var = "ID",
  method    = "NM",
  max.iters = 1000
)
summary(poislind.mod)
